chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from one of his companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), that he said:
Regarding a man who married two sisters in one marriage contract, he said: He has the choice; he may keep whichever of the two he desires and release the other.
And he said regarding a man who had a slave girl, so he slept with her, then bought her mother or her daughter: She is not permissible for him [ever].
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man marries two sisters at the same time or buys the mother of his slave concubine?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between temporary prohibition (due to simultaneous marriage) and permanent prohibition (due to consummation with a slave and subsequent purchase of her relative). It highlights the Shia juristic principle that while marrying two sisters in one contract allows for the retention of either, consummation with a slave girl creates an eternal barrier if her mother or daughter is later acquired, reflecting the specific application of lineage and union rules in classical fiqh.
